title: Jude and the Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Tamsin Eriksen is hired by a dying stranger, Marlowe Vane, who pays triple fees to prove that his sister Lark — declared dead seven years ago — was never murdered at all, because if she was, the killer is Marlowe himself, the sole beneficiary of her estate. Digging into a will that was probated in secret, Tamsin uncovers a forged death certificate, a second will hidden inside a family trust, and evidence that Lark staged her own disappearance to escape a marriage built on blackmail. As Tamsin closes in on the truth, Marlowe's deadline tightens: he is dying, and whoever holds the true will at his death inherits everything — including the motive to make sure Lark stays dead. Tamsin must find Lark alive before Marlowe's heirs do, and in the final confrontation at the decaying Vane estate, Tamsin chooses love over duty, burning the forged will and giving Lark her life back while surrendering the fee, the reputation, and the invisibility they spent a career protecting.
about_author: August Blackwood is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's last words before starting to write their own. They live in a coastal town where fog is a legal excuse for almost anything.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid Too Much
chapters.summary: Tamsin Eriksen, a meticulous estate lawyer with a reputation for closing anything, is visited by the gaunt, dying Marlowe Vane, who offers triple fees to prove his sister's seven-year-old murder never happened. His condition: Tamsin must never learn why he needs it undone. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: unease wrapped in professional confidence — the first crack in Tamsin's invisibility.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Tamsin pulls the probate file on Lark Vane's death and finds a sealed will probated in secret, signed by a notary who died a month later. The estate passed entirely to Marlowe — no contest, no questions. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the thrill of an anomaly turning to dread as the file's neatness feels rehearsed.

chapters.title: The House on Coldwater Hill
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits the decaying Vane estate, ostensibly to inventory assets, and meets the housekeeper, Odile, who mentions — casually, terribly — that fresh flowers are still placed in Lark's room every week. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the house feels inhabited by an absence, and Tamsin begins to suspect the dead sister isn't done speaking.

chapters.title: Marlowe's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Marlowe summons Tamsin, drunk, and nearly admits something about the night Lark vanished before Odile interrupts. He gives Tamsin a key to Lark's old study and a deadline: the case closes before his heart does. POV: Marlowe. Emotional beat: guilt so heavy it masquerades as arrogance; the reader begins to pity the man they suspect.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: A graphologist confirms Lark's signature on the death-adjacent documents was traced — by someone with access to her correspondence. Tamsin realizes the forgery happened inside the house, not at a lawyer's office. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the professional satisfaction of proof curdling into fear of what the proof implies.

chapters.title: Odile's Flowers
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Odile, who reveals she was paid anonymously for seven years to keep Lark's room ready — and that the payments come from an account Tamsin recognizes: the Vane family trust. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: loyalty and terror intertwined; Odile knows more than she'll say and is deciding whether Tamsin is safe to tell.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Inside Lark's locked study, Tamsin finds a hidden compartment containing a second will — Lark's own, dated after the murder, leaving everything to a name Tamsin doesn't recognize. It's legally valid and changes everything. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead woman has outmaneuvered everyone, including her own lawyer.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Reading the File
chapters.summary: Tamsin's office is searched; the second will's location is compromised. A stranger with a lawyer's polish, Cassian Roth, introduces himself as counsel for the Vane trust — and warns Tamsin off with impeccable politeness. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the hunted feeling of being visible for the first time in a career built on not being seen.

chapters.title: The Marriage Built on Blackmail
chapters.summary: Digging into Lark's past, Tamsin discovers she was married to Cassian Roth — a marriage sustained by his leverage over a secret she kept. The 'murder' looks less like violence and more like an exit strategy. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration for Lark, and the first flicker of personal investment beyond the fee.

chapters.title: Marlowe Deteriorates
chapters.summary: Marlowe, failing fast, tells Tamsin a partial truth: he helped Lark disappear to protect her from Cassian, but someone in the house betrayed her plan, and Lark has been silent ever since. He doesn't know if she's alive. POV: Marlowe. Emotional beat: a confession that raises more questions than it settles; love expressed as complicity.

chapters.title: The Account in the Trust
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces the anonymous payments and finds they were authorized by a signature that matches the forged one — meaning either Lark is alive and paying, or someone is keeping her ghost on payroll. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: hope and manipulation indistinguishable; Tamsin can no longer tell who is running this case.

chapters.title: Cassian Makes His Offer
chapters.summary: Cassian offers Tamsin a partnership and the case of a lifetime if the second will 'goes missing.' He mentions Tamsin's own buried past — proof he's been digging too. POV: Cassian. Emotional beat: seduction and threat in one breath; the reader sees how Lark was once cornered the same way.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Tamsin's own history — a case closed too neatly years ago, a client destroyed by Tamsin's refusal to look deeper. The reason Tamsin never takes a case they can't close. POV: Tamsin (past and present). Emotional beat: the mask cracks; this case has stopped being professional.

chapters.title: The Night Lark Left
chapters.summary: Reconstruction: Tamsin pieces together the disappearance — a boat, a storm, a witness who saw two people on the water, and a body that was never actually found. The 'murder' was staged by someone who wanted it believed. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the case inverts; the question is no longer who killed Lark, but who needed her dead on paper.

chapters.title: Odile Breaks
chapters.summary: Odile, terrified after Cassian visits the house, gives Tamsin a letter Lark left behind — addressed to whoever finally asked the right question. It contains a location and a warning: trust no one who benefits from the will. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: release after years of silence; the housekeeper's loyalty finally points somewhere.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse at Greyhaven
chapters.summary: Following the letter, Tamsin travels to a remote coastal lighthouse and finds evidence someone has been living there — recent, careful, invisible. Then footsteps. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: breathless suspense; the case everyone swore was closed is about to open its eyes.

chapters.title: Lark
chapters.summary: Tamsin meets Lark Vane — alive, hardened, and furious that anyone found her. She explains the staging, Cassian's blackmail, and why she let her brother believe in her death: to keep him and everyone else safe. POV: Lark. Emotional beat: grief and relief colliding; a ghost who never wanted to be resurrected.

chapters.title: The Deadline Moves
chapters.summary: Marlowe is hospitalized. Cassian, sensing the end, moves to have the trust dissolved and the estate transferred before any will can surface. Tamsin has days, not weeks. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the trap closing from every side; duty says hand over the will, love of the truth says burn the whole machine.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Lark return to the estate to confront Marlowe one last time. Cassian is waiting, having anticipated them, and forces a standoff over the second will — with Marlowe's dying wish as the stakes. POV: alternating Tamsin and Lark. Emotional beat: the climax; love against duty made literal, a gun, a will, and a dying man's last honest hour.

chapters.title: Marlowe's Last Will
chapters.summary: Marlowe, lucid at the end, dictates a new will on record — disinheriting Cassian's control, acknowledging Lark alive, and absolving Tamsin of every obligation but one: tell the truth, even the ugly parts. Cassian is exposed with the blackmail evidence. POV: Marlowe, then Tamsin. Emotional beat: catharsis; the man who paid to un-prove a murder finally gets the truth he actually wanted.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Burns
chapters.summary: Tamsin destroys the forged documents, files the true will, and walks away from the fee — and from the firm that demands they close cases, not questions. Cassian is arrested; Odile keeps the house and the flowers. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: quiet devastation and liberation; the invisible lawyer steps into the light at a cost.

chapters.title: The Case That Stayed Open
chapters.summary: Months later, Lark visits Tamsin's small new practice — not as a client, but as something gentler. The case is closed, the file is thin, and Tamsin, for the first time, leaves one question deliberately unanswered: what they might become. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: warm resolution; identity rebuilt not around duty, but around the choice to love against it.
